scope: origin/main..HEAD on 002-subscription-page: mvp_payments/money.py, mvp_payments/namespaces/drf_stripe_records.py, mvp_payments/namespaces/drf_stripe.py, mvp_payments/views.py, mvp_payments/contributions.py, mvp_payments/static/mvp_payments/drf_stripe/billing_portal.js, mvp_payments/templates/cotton/drf_stripe/*, mvp_payments/templates/mvp_payments/drf_stripe/subscription.html, demo/*, docs/subscription-page.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, tests/* — against specs/002-subscription-page/spec.md, decisions.md, CONSTITUTION.md (Articles X-XVII), CONTEXT.md, and the resolved drf-stripe-subscription package under the project's virtualenv. Combined correctness + spec-compliance lens per craft-review; each finding's claim is prefixed with its effective lens since the schema carries one lens at the top level.

findings.claim: [correctness] Money.exponent compares the recorded currency code against ZERO_DECIMAL/THREE_DECIMAL as uppercase literals, but the drf-stripe-subscription backend this page reads always stores the currency code lowercase, exactly as Stripe's API returns it. Every zero-decimal currency (JPY, KRW, VND, ...) and three-decimal currency (BHD, KWD, ...) therefore falls through to the 2-decimal default and renders the wrong amount in every real installation — not a hypothetical input, the backend's own normal behaviour.
findings.evidence: mvp_payments/money.py:335-339 — `if self.currency in self.ZERO_DECIMAL:` / `if self.currency in self.THREE_DECIMAL:`, both frozensets holding only uppercase codes (money.py:306-329). mvp_payments/namespaces/drf_stripe_records.py:516 passes `price.currency` straight through with no case normalisation: `Money(minor_units=price.price, currency=price.currency)`. The backend's own sync code writes that field verbatim from Stripe's API object, unmodified: .venv/.../drf_stripe/stripe_webhooks/price.py:23 (`currency = data.object.currency`, written via `update_or_create`) and .venv/.../drf_stripe/stripe_api/products.py:74. Stripe's API always returns currency codes lowercase, confirmed by the backend's own `StripeCurrency` enum (.venv/.../drf_stripe/stripe_models/currency.py), e.g. `JPY = 'jpy'`, `USD = 'usd'`. Reproduced directly: `Money(minor_units=500000, currency='jpy').exponent` returns `2` (should be `0`) and `str(Money(minor_units=500000, currency='jpy'))` renders `'5,000.00 jpy'` where the correct reading of 500000 JPY minor units is `500,000 JPY` — a 100x error. Every test and fixture in this diff masks the defect by using uppercase currency literals that never occur in a real installation: tests/factories.py:63 (`currency = "USD"`), tests/test_money.py (all four cases use `"USD"`/`"JPY"`/`"BHD"`), demo/management/commands/seed_demo.py (`"currency": "USD"` / `"currency": "JPY"`).
findings.reproduction: cd django-mvp-payments && poetry run python -c "import django, os, sys; os.environ.setdefault('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE','tests.settings'); sys.path[:0]=['.','tests']; django.setup(); from mvp_payments.money import Money; print(Money(minor_units=500000, currency='jpy').exponent); print(str(Money(minor_units=500000, currency='jpy')))" — prints `2` and `5,000.00 jpy` instead of `0` and `500,000 JPY`.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare against the normalised currency in `exponent` (`self.currency.upper() in self.ZERO_DECIMAL`, same for THREE_DECIMAL) and render the currency code uppercased in `__str__`, so the lookup and the display are correct regardless of the case the backend recorded. Add a `tests/test_money.py` case using a lowercase currency (`Money(minor_units=500000, currency="jpy")` → `"500,000 JPY"`) so the suite stops relying on fixture data that never occurs in production. This is Article XVI's own named worst case: "A wrong price on a pricing page is the one defect in this package that costs a reader real money."

findings.claim: [spec-compliance] `<c-drf-stripe.portal-link>` does not actually render correctly from its attributes alone (FR-012, SC-006, docs/subscription-page.md:104 "each one renders on its own given its attributes"): its CSRF token is read from the ambient `{{ csrf_token }}` context variable rather than declared as a prop, so it silently renders empty whenever the component is rendered outside a `RequestContext` — the exact 'placed in an unrelated template' scenario US-5/SC-006 exists to guarantee. `billing_portal.js` then posts with an empty `X-CSRFToken` header, which Django's CSRF protection rejects, and the reader sees a generic 'could not be reached' failure for a control that looked correctly rendered.
findings.evidence: mvp_payments/templates/cotton/drf_stripe/portal_link.html:14 reads `{{ csrf_token }}` with no corresponding `<c-vars>` entry (only `endpoint` is declared, line 13). Reproduced directly by rendering the component with a plain `django.template.Context` (the same construction `cotton_render_string` — the fixture the diff's own standalone test `test_portal_link_renders_inside_an_unrelated_template` (tests/test_components/test_drf_stripe.py:291-300) uses) builds: `data-csrf-token=""` comes back empty. The same render through a `RequestContext` (what a normal Django view produces) correctly populates the token, which is why `TestPortalLink`'s `cotton_render`-based test (tests/test_components/test_drf_stripe.py:189-204, using the request-carrying `cotton_render` fixture) passes and gave no signal of the gap. `test_portal_link_renders_inside_an_unrelated_template` only asserts `data-endpoint` is present, not the csrf-token attribute, so nothing in the suite catches this.
findings.reproduction: cd django-mvp-payments && poetry run python -c "import django, os, sys; os.environ.setdefault('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE','tests.settings'); sys.path[:0]=['.','tests']; django.setup(); from django.template import Context, Template; from django.test import RequestFactory; from django_cotton.compiler_regex import CottonCompiler; c=CottonCompiler(); r=RequestFactory().get('/'); t=Template(c.process('<c-drf-stripe.portal-link :endpoint=\"endpoint\" />')); ctx=Context({'endpoint':'/api/stripe/customer-portal/','request':r}); ctx.request=r; html=t.render(ctx); import re; print(re.search(r'data-csrf-token=\"([^\"]*)\"', html).group(1))" — prints an empty string.
findings.suggested_fix: The four other components in this feature genuinely need nothing but their declared attributes; only this one has a hidden dependency. Smallest fix that matches the stated contract: declare the requirement rather than hide it — either add `csrf_token` to `<c-vars>` so the caller must supply it explicitly (matching how `endpoint` is already handled, and matching FR-012's own wording), or, if depending on RequestContext is accepted as this component's one exception, say so plainly in docs/subscription-page.md next to its entry (currently line 132-139) and stop claiming at line 104 that all six 'render on its own given its attributes' without qualification. Either way, extend the standalone test to assert the csrf-token attribute is non-empty so a regression here is caught.

notes: billing_portal.js has no debounce or disabled-state on the button while a request is in flight, so a double click fires two portal-session POSTs; harmless (Stripe's endpoint tolerates repeat calls, the browser navigates on whichever response resolves first) but worth a one-line guard if this file ever grows a second control.

Looked hard and found clean: the ZERO_DECIMAL/THREE_DECIMAL currency-code sets themselves are correct against Stripe's published list (16 zero-decimal, 7 three-decimal, matching money.py exactly) — the defect is the case-sensitive comparison (REV-001), not the table's contents. The portal-withholding guarantee (D5/D11/ADR-0007) is airtight in SubscriptionPageView.get_context_data, not merely in the template — billing_portal_endpoint is None whenever subscriptions is empty regardless of what a project's overridden template does, verified against drf_stripe's StripeCustomerPortal/get_or_create_stripe_user chain. frequency_display's interval parsing correctly anticipates Stripe's own lowercase interval convention (day/week/month/year), unlike Money's currency table. The N+1 risk DR-002 flagged at design review is closed: SubscriptionReader.for_user uses select_related/prefetch_related on a real queryset (StripeUser.current_subscription_items is a QuerySet property, not a materialised list), and tests/test_views.py's CaptureQueriesContext-based test asserts a constant query count independent of item count.
